q: What type of flashing is formed from metal or elastomeric sheeting and is secured to a wall, curb, pipe, or other surface to cover and protect the upper edge of a base flashing and its fasteners?
n: Counterflashing is fixed to the wall, curb or pipe above the base flashing and laps down over its top edge and fasteners, so water cannot run behind it. Source: SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual; NRCA Roofing Manual.

q: What beveled piece at a roof-to-wall junction gives the flashing a smooth transition?
n: A cant strip is a beveled (usually 45°) strip at the roof-to-wall angle, so the membrane or flashing turns up smoothly instead of cracking at a sharp 90° bend. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What wall type is needed when a basement is built?
n: Basement walls hold back the surrounding earth and groundwater pressure, so they must be designed as retaining walls. Source: NSCP 2015 Chapter 3 (lateral soil pressure); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is the most suitable approach for exterior basement walls below grade?
n: Positive-side waterproofing goes on the outside (wet) face of basement walls, stopping water before it enters the concrete. It is the most effective approach where the outside can be reached. Source: ACI 515.2R; Henshell, The Manual of Below-Grade Waterproofing Systems.

q: What is the best material to waterproof the outside of a basement wall before backfill?
n: Bituminous (modified bitumen) sheet membranes stand up to soil contact and hydrostatic pressure, so they are a standard exterior basement wall waterproofing, with a protection board before backfill. Source: ASTM D6164/D6222; Henshell, The Manual of Below-Grade Waterproofing Systems.

q: Which waterproofing approach is used when access to the exterior of a basement wall is not possible?
n: When the outside of a basement wall cannot be reached (existing buildings, walls against neighbors), waterproofing is applied on the inside (negative side), usually as crystalline or cementitious coatings that resist water pressure. Source: ACI 515.2R; Henshell, The Manual of Below-Grade Waterproofing Systems.

q: What is laid along the base of basement walls to collect and carry groundwater away?
n: A French (footing) drain is a perforated pipe in gravel, wrapped in filter fabric, along the base of the wall. It collects groundwater and carries it to a sump or outfall, relieving water pressure. Source: ACI 515.2R; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (foundation drainage).

q: Elastoseal is made by which company?
n: Elastoseal is a waterproofing and sealant product line of Pioneer Adhesives Inc. Source: Pioneer Adhesives company website.

q: Which brand makes the cementitious waterproofing Plexibond?
n: Plexibond is Boysen's cementitious waterproofing (acrylic-modified cement coating) used under tiles and on wet areas. Source: Boysen company website.

q: What local brand in the Philippines is commonly associated with waterproofing membranes and sealants for roof decks and wet areas?
n: Bostik, distributed widely in the Philippines, is best known for sealants, adhesives and waterproofing membranes for roof decks and wet areas. Boysen is paint and Holcim is cement. Source: Bostik Philippines product literature.

q: Which of the following is a two-component, flexible cementitious waterproofing membrane manufactured by Buildrite?
n: Flexicrete is Buildrite's two-component flexible cementitious waterproofing membrane. Source: Buildrite company product literature.

q: Which of these insulation materials is lightest?
n: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam is about 98% air, with densities around 10–30 kg/m³, lighter than rock wool or fiberglass batts. Source: ASTM C578 (rigid cellular polystyrene); insulation manufacturer data.

q: Which of these is the most expensive insulation?
n: Polyurethane foam insulation costs the most of the four per unit area, though it also gives the highest R-value per thickness. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Insulation Materials.

q: Which insulation is commonly fitted between wall studs?
n: Fiberglass batts are pre-cut to stud and joist spacing and friction-fit between wall studs. They are the most common cavity insulation. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Types of Insulation; ASTM C665.

q: Which insulation is made from polyethylene?
n: Polyethylene is made into film membranes used as vapor barriers and reflective-foil backing. Of the choices given, "membrane" is the polyethylene product. Source: ASTM E1745 (polyethylene vapor retarders).

q: Which insulation suits people with asthma best?
n: Polyester fiber insulation (recycled PET) does not shed itchy glass or mineral fibers and has no binders or formaldehyde, so it is the best choice for people with asthma or allergies. Source: Insulation manufacturer literature (polyester batts); US EPA indoor air guidance.

q: Of these four, which insulation costs the most to install?
n: Spray polyurethane foam costs the most to install: it needs special equipment, trained applicators and protective measures, while batts are installed by hand. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Insulation Materials.

q: Which insulation seals walls against both moisture and air?
n: Spray polyurethane foam expands to fill every gap and crack, acting as both an air seal and (closed-cell) a moisture barrier, as well as insulation. Source: US DOE Energy Saver; ASTM C1029 (spray polyurethane).

q: Which insulation material has the highest resistance to water vapor?
n: Extruded polystyrene (XPS) has a closed-cell skin with very low water absorption and vapor permeance, the highest moisture resistance among common foam boards. Source: ASTM C578; insulation manufacturer data.

q: Which insulation is commonly used under roofing?
n: Reflective foil laminates (often with bubble or foam cores) are the standard insulation under roof sheets in the Philippines, blocking radiant heat from the hot roof. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), roof insulation; manufacturer literature.

q: Which insulation has the lowest R-value on its own but performs well with an air cavity?
n: Foil has almost no R-value by itself. It works by its low emissivity, which only reduces heat transfer when it faces an air cavity. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (reflective insulation); ASTM C1313.

q: What is the correct order of layers in a roof system, from top?
n: From the top: roof sheet, then the insulation blanket laid over the purlins, then the purlins themselves. The insulation sits right under the sheet. Source: Insulation and metal roofing manufacturer installation guides.

q: Which insulation type typically does not come with a 50-year warranty?
n: Glass wool, rock wool and Earthwool are inorganic and are often sold with very long (up to 50-year) warranties. Spray foam warranties are typically shorter and depend on the applicator. Source: Insulation manufacturer warranty literature (Knauf, Rockwool).

q: What is the most affordable roof insulation suited to the tropics?
n: In the tropics, radiant heat from a hot roof is the main load, and reflective foil blocks it at the lowest cost per square meter. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015); ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals.

q: Which insulation contains about 50% recycled PET?
n: Polyester insulation batts are made largely from recycled PET bottles, often about half or more. Source: Polyester insulation manufacturer literature.

q: In a vaulted ceiling, where does insulation go?
n: A vaulted (cathedral) ceiling has no attic, so insulation is placed between the rafters, with ventilation space above, under the roof deck. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Insulation in Cathedral Ceilings.
